metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Shouldn't be out too long
metadata.description: Harvey (knee) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, but his injury isn't considered severe or long term, Sam Jane of The Denver Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Harvey was a mid-week addition to the injury report, listed as limited Thursday and absent Friday. It sounds like he may only miss a game or two, but that could impact his role down the stretch if rookie Jonah Coleman takes advantage of the opportunity ahead. Coleman took half of the snaps and half of the backfield opportunities last week in his first game back from injured reserve, while Harvey was limited to a 25 percent snap share and five touches, relying on a 52-yard TD reception to salvage his fantasy day. Harvey's absence could free up a few more snaps and touches for Coleman or J.K. Dobbins.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey (knee) ruled out Sunday
metadata.description: RJ Harvey has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: Harvey was a late addition to the injury report on Thursday. Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins should both step into bigger roles in the Broncos backfield.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Ruled out for Sunday's game
metadata.description: Harvey (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette reports.
metadata.analysis: After logging a limited practice Thursday, Harvey will now miss Sunday's divisional clash with the rival Chiefs. Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins should handle most of the backfield work for the Broncos, but Tyler Badie could see some pass-game action.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey's Knee Injury Not Believed to be Serious
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey's knee injury is not believed to be severe or hold him out long-term, a source told Sam Jane of The Denver Post. Harvey was ruled out of the team's game on Sunday against the division-rival Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8 after popping up on Thursday's injury report and failing to practice on Friday, but this is encouraging news for the second-year back. The 25-year-old needs to be removed from starting lineups this weekend against KC, but it seems possible that he could return as early as next weekend on the road against the Carolina Panthers. With the former second-rounder from Central Florida out in Week 8, rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins will split backfield duties against the Chiefs. However, when Harvey returns, Coleman could have more of a stranglehold on backfield touches in Denver, which might make Harvey harder to trust as an RB3/flex in PPR formats. Harvey has only 24 carries this year for 87 yards and a touchdown on the ground, adding 25 catches for 217 yards and another score on 28 targets as a receiver through six games.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Ruled Out for Week 8 Against Chiefs
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey (knee) was added to the Week 8 injury report on Thursday with a knee injury and has now been ruled out for Sunday's clash against the division-rival Kansas City Chiefs after not practicing on Friday, according to Zac Stevens of DNVR Sports. It is a pretty big development for Denver's backfield, as J.K. Dobbins and rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman will now be set up for bigger workloads as they share the backfield against a formidable Chiefs defense. Harvey's next chance to return will be in a Week 9 matchup on the road against the Carolina Panthers. If Coleman is still floating around your league's waiver wire, he should be considered a must-add with clear RB2 upside this weekend in a bigger role after head coach Sean Payton said the team will look to get the rookie more involved. The 25-year-old Harvey still has value in point-per-reception leagues -- he has 25 catches on 28 targets for 217 yards and one touchdown as a receiver -- but Coleman's return from Injured Reserve definitely puts a dent in Harvey's rest-of-season outlook in Denver's backfield.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey (knee) added to injury report Thursday
metadata.description: RJ Harvey (knee) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Harvey is a new addition to Denver's injury report, being listed with a knee issue of some kind that left him limited at practice. This is a situation worth monitoring heading into the weekend, as J.K. Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman will both see more work if Harvey is sidelined against the Chiefs.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Added to injury report Thursday
metadata.description: Harvey (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Harvey wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so it's unclear if his limitations a day later stem from Denver's initial practice or were the result of an issue the running back encountered Thursday. In any case, added context with regard to Harvey's status for Sunday's game against the Chiefs will arrive no later than Friday. If available this weekend, Harvey will contend with J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman for Denver's Week 8 backfield touches.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Added to Injury Report, Limited on Thursday
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey (knee) was added to the Week 8 injury report on Thursday and was listed as a limited participant in practice due to a knee injury, according to Zac Stevens of DNVR Sports. Harvey's status is worth keeping a close eye on heading into a big Week 8 divisional contest at home against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. The 25-year-old noticeably played a season-low 26% of the offensive snaps and had only five touches (three carries for six yards and two catches for 54 yards and a touchdown) in the Week 7 win over the Arizona Cardinals with rookie fourth-round RB Jonah Coleman returning from Injured Reserve. Head coach Sean Payton has made it clear that he wants to get Coleman more involved in this three-headed rushing attack that also includes J.K. Dobbins, so that is obviously bad news for Harvey's fantasy ceiling moving forward. If Harvey's knee injury is serious enough to keep him sidelined against the Chiefs, Coleman will essentially be a borderline must-start RB in his second game back from an ankle injury that he suffered in Week 2. Harvey has not done much as a runner in six games, averaging 3.6 yards per carry on 24 carries, but he has been a PPR flex with 25 catches on 28 targets for 217 yards and one touchdown through the air.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Scores 52-Yard Touchdown in Week 7
metadata.description: RJ Harvey rushed three times for six yards, while catching both of his targets for 54 yards and one touchdown in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Cardinals in Week 7
metadata.analysis: Harvey turned a short pass from Bo Nix into a 52-yard touchdown for his biggest play of the afternoon. The touchdown saved an otherwise quiet day, as Harvey received just five touches with Jonah Coleman returning to the lineup. Harvey remains involved as a receiver, but Coleman's return adds another player to an already crowded Denver backfield. The former is in flex territory.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Catches 52-yard TD in win
metadata.description: Harvey rushed three times for six yards while catching both of his targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: Harvey did most of his damage on a 52-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, but he was quiet otherwise. Jonah Coleman turned nine carries and two catches into 69 scrimmage yards in the rookie's return from an ankle injury, while J.K. Dobbins scored a touchdown on one of the latter's six rushing attempts, so Denver has a three-man backfield rotation going ahead of a Week 8 home game against the Chiefs. Harvey has a path to consistent targets as a pass catcher out of the backfield, especially if he continues to capitalize on those opportunities like he did Sunday.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Leads Broncos in Receiving Yards in Week 7
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey did not do much as a rusher in his team's Week 7 win over the Arizona Cardinals, logging just three carries for six yards. However, the second-year back made a major impact as a receiver, hauling in two catches for 54 yards and a touchdown on two targets. Harvey has emerged as a critical piece of the Broncos' pass game in 2026, recording 25 catches for 217 yards and two touchdowns on 28 targets across six games played. Harvey figures to split carries with fellow Denver backs J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman most weeks, which caps his upside as a rusher and fantasy running back overall. Still, Harvey's work as a pass-catcher makes him an intriguing deep-league PPR flex option for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Offers PPR Flex Upside With an Uneven Receiving Role
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey is a PPR flex for Sunday's visit to the Arizona Cardinals, with an uneven receiving role. He has 23 receptions for 163 yards in five appearances, 16 of them against the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers and none against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 5. The second-year back rebounded against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6 with three catches for 31 yards and six carries for 25 yards and a touchdown. J.K. Dobbins is still handling the larger rushing workload, Harvey has received just 21 carries through six weeks, and Jonah Coleman's potential return from an ankle injury adds another variable.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Re-Establishes PPR Appeal With Receiving Work
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey has caught more passes than he has logged rushing attempts this season, with 23 receptions for 163 yards on 26 targets compared with 21 carries for 81 yards across five appearances. After managing one target and no catches in Week 5, Harvey caught three of four targets for a team-high 31 yards in Denver's 17-14 overtime win over Seattle. He added six carries for 25 yards and his first touchdown of 2026, but J.K. Dobbins handled 17 rushing attempts and remains the lead option on the ground. Harvey's 10-catch Week 4 game accounts for a big chunk of his receiving production, which makes his weekly target total hard to trust. His pass-catching role still gives him deeper-league PPR flex appeal ahead of Week 7 against Arizona. That outlook comes with an added wrinkle, as Jonah Coleman (ankle) has been designated to return from injured reserve and was back at practice Wednesday, although he hasn't been activated yet.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey bounces back in Thursday win
metadata.description: RJ Harvey ran six times for 25 yards and a touchdown while also catching three of four targets for 31 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 win over Seattle on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: After going silent in Week 5, Harvey got back on track in Week 6, scoring a touchdown and even leading the Broncos in receiving. That last bit is a huge indictment of the Broncos' passing game, which has struggled mightily this year. Harvey is an RB3 at best right now, but if you have other options with a more stable floor who can start, that's likely the best course of action.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Solid production with nine touches
metadata.description: Harvey rushed six times for 25 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 31 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Harvey finished with a team-high receiving yardage total on a night when Bo Nix threw for only 107 yards, and the second-year back made key complementary contributions on the ground as well. Harvey scored his first touchdown of the season on a one-yard run with 5:15 remaining in the second quarter, while his rushing yardage total tied a season high. Harvey projects to remain in his change-of-pace role when the Broncos visit the Cardinals in a Week 7 matchup on Sunday, Oct. 25.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Back to Irrelevance in Week 5
metadata.description: After a notable performance in Week 4, Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey was a non-factor during his team's win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Harvey recorded 17 total touches, including 10 receptions, for 93 total yards during a loss to the San Francisco 49ers two weeks ago, but failed to follow that solid effort up with another productive performance against Los Angeles. He finished the win over the Chargers with just three carries for seven yards and without a reception on just a single target. Still, Harvey remains just two spots behind Broncos starting running back J.K. Dobbins in RotoBaller's weekly rankings as RB28. Harvey is projected to score eight fantasy points in a Week 6 matchup with the Seattle Seahawks.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey a non-factor in Week 5 win
metadata.description: RJ Harvey gained seven yards on three carries and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 23-17 win over the Chargers.
metadata.analysis: A week after coming up with 10 catches, Harvey was blanked in the passing game and limited to just three touches Sunday afternoon. J.K. Dobbins shouldered the load out of the backfield in this victory, making it clear that Harvey is still firmly behind him on the depth chart. Harvey is a worthwhile handcuff to stash, but he is game-script dependent and unreliable as long as Dobbins remains healthy.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Logs one target in Week 5
metadata.description: Harvey notched three carries for seven yards and didn't haul in his only target during Sunday's 23-17 road win versus the Chargers.
metadata.analysis: After being targeted a whopping 17 times over the previous two games, Harvey experienced a change in fortunes Sunday as no Bronco earned more than WR Jaylen Waddle's five looks from QB Bo Nix. Harvey hasn't been able to get anything going on the ground this season (3.7 YPC) in his four appearances while Dobbins has earned the more consistent workload (13.8 touches per game), leaving the former a distant second in the pecking order out of Denver's backfield.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey No-Shows Versus Chargers
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey was held to just seven rushing yards on three carries (2.3 yards per carry) in a 23-17 Week 5 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers. Harvey saw just one target in the passing game, but did not record a reception. Harvey's lack of usage in Week 5 comes as a surprise after he received 10 targets in the passing game and tallied 10 receptions for 68 yards, to go along with 25 rushing yards, in a Week 4 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. However, the Broncos had a tough day through the air against the Chargers, as quarterback Bo Nix amassed just 123 passing yards. J.K. Dobbins led the Broncos with 18 carries for 68 yards (3.8 yards per carry) and a touchdown against L.A. Dobbins also had two catches for six yards. Dobbins out-snapped Harvey 32 to 23 and out-touched Harvey 20 to 3 in Week 5. Harvey has been inefficient on the ground in 2026, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, but he should remain involved as a pass-catcher.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Coming Off Productive Effort
metadata.description: He hasn't been used much in the running game, but Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey has been a significant factor in the passing game to start the year. Harvey is coming off his most productive performance of the season, finishing a loss to the San Francisco 49ers with 10 receptions on 10 targets for 68 yards. He now has 20 receptions for 132 yards on the season, along with 49 yards rushing on 12 carries, an average of 4.1 yards per carry. As a result, Harvey is ranked two spots ahead of his backfield mate, J.K. Dobbins, as RotoBaller's RB25 entering Week 5. Harvey is projected to score 10 fantasy points against the Los Angeles Chargers, who allowed Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson to finish a Week 4 Seattle win with three receptions for 39 yards and a touchdown.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Flaunting Receiving Upside
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey has been central to the offense's passing attack, leading the team with 20 receptions. The second-year pro has capitalized on quarterback Bo Nix's willingness to throw it underneath, hauling in at least four receptions in each of his appearances. Harvey has been excellent; only he and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (16) have hit double digits in catches, and he could remain frequently utilized if wideout Pat Bryant (ankle) misses Sunday's divisional matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. Some of the offensive flow may change with head coach Sean Payton slated for playcalling duties, but Harvey is trending positively despite limited production on the ground. Encouragingly, he's outpaced backfield mate J.K. Dobbins in snaps twice in three games.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey, J.K. Dobbins struggle in loss Sunday
metadata.description: J.K. Dobbins rushed 11 times for 40 yards, while RJ Harvey had seven carries for 25 yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Harvey also caught 10 passes for 68 yards out of the backfield.
metadata.analysis: Denver couldn't get much going on the ground, with Dobbins and Harvey combining for just 65 rushing yards. Dobbins continued to handle more of the rushing work, but Harvey was much more involved as a receiver and ended up leading the Broncos in both receptions and receiving yards. The backfield remains a split, with Dobbins having the better chance at early-down work and Harvey carrying more upside in the passing game.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Massive receiving workload in loss
metadata.description: Harvey rushed seven times for 25 yards and secured all 10 targets for 68 yards in the Broncos' 24-14 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. He also returned two kickoffs for 64 yards and committed a fumble recovered by Denver.
metadata.analysis: Harvey was only four carries behind J.K. Dobbins on an afternoon when game script eventually turned against the run in the second half, but the second-year back saw the biggest workload of any Broncos pass catcher. Harvey led the team across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and both his catch and target tallies were also career highs. The early exit of Pat Bryant with an ankle injury may have had at least a nominal influence on boosting Harvey's pass-catching opportunities, but the latter is highly valued for his receiving capabilities overall and should retain a solid complementary role in a Week 5 road matchup against the Chargers next Sunday.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey a Factor in Broncos Passing Game
metadata.description: While he hasn't done much work on the ground this season, totaling only five carries for 24 yards through two games played, Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey has been a factor in the passing game. Harvey is second among Broncos pass catchers in both targets (11) and receptions (10), while his 64 yards receiving are fourth on the team. This past week, Harvey hauled in six receptions for 41 yards during a win over the Los Angeles Rams. In Week 4, the Broncos face a San Francisco 49ers defense that allowed Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love to record five receptions for 19 yards and a touchdown last Sunday. Harvey is RotoBaller's 28th-ranked running back and is projected to score nine fantasy points against San Francisco.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Emerging as a Factor in Broncos Passing Game
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey has barely been involved as a runner, but Denver keeps finding him in the passing game. Harvey returned from a hamstring injury in Week 3 and caught six of seven targets for 41 yards against the Rams. That came after he caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in the opener. Through two appearances, he has 10 receptions on 11 targets despite only five carries. J.K. Dobbins is still handling the bulk of the rushing work, but his start has been uneven. He has 121 yards on 35 carries, an average of 3.5 yards per attempt, and has yet to score on the ground. Harvey is not taking that job away right now. The receiving work still gives him a real path to fantasy value, though, and it is a role he handled well as a rookie with 47 catches for 356 yards and five touchdowns. If Denver keeps leaning on him in passing situations, Harvey can keep climbing even without a major shift in carries.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey (concussion) off injury report
metadata.description: RJ Harvey is off the injury report on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Harvey was checked for a concussion in Week. He will be good to go in his complimentary role next to J.K. Dobbins.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey hauls in six passes Sunday
metadata.description: RJ Harvey hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 41 yards and rushed the ball two times for six yards in Sunday night's 30-26 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: The young running back was able to make his return to the lineup on Sunday night after missing last week's game due to a hamstring issue. He looked okay in his first game back, seeing a lot of involvement as a receiver but very little work as a rusher against the Rams. His role will continue to be limited for the team moving forward, though he might have to step up and play a bigger role than usual with Jonah Coleman (ankle) set to miss several weeks at least.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Seven targets, two carries in Week 3
metadata.description: Harvey (hamstring) rushed twice for six yards while catching six of seven targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams.
metadata.analysis: Harvey didn't see much involvement on the ground but tied for the team lead in targets in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. He was evaluated for a concussion in the second half and cleared to return, though Harvey had just one touch after that point. J.K. Dobbins is likely to keep working as Denver's primary rushing option in Week 4 against the 49ers, especially with rookie fourth-round pick Jonah Coleman (ankle) on IR, while Harvey remains the preferred running back in passing situations.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Cleared to return vs. Rams
metadata.description: Harvey has been cleared to return to Sunday's game against the Rams after passing a concussion evaluation, Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette reports.
metadata.analysis: Harvey was evaluated for a concussion in the third quarter but has been cleared to return to action. He rejoins a Denver backfield that also includes J.K. Dobbins and Tyler Badie in the second half of Sunday night's game against the Rams.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Getting evaluated for concussion
metadata.description: Harvey is being evaluated for a concussion, Parker Gabriel of the Denver Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Harvey was taken to the blue injury tent, and eventually to the locker room, to be evaluated for a concussion in the third quarter of Sunday's game against the Rams. The 2025 second-round pick will need to pass the evaluation to return to the game. J.K. Dobbins and Tyler Badie are Denver's available running backs. Harvey had two carries for six yards and caught five of six targets for 39 yards prior to coming off the field.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Cleared to Return on Sunday
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey (head) was taken out of the game to be evaluated for a concussion during the second half of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. Harvey has cleared concussion protocol and is available to return for the rest of Sunday's game, per Zac Stevens. This is a big boost for the Broncos offense, with Harvey having five receptions when he was bounced out of the game. He is expected to be an important piece to the offense during the final stretch of the game. Fantasy managers don't need to worry about a concussion with Harvey at the moment.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey is Being Evaluated for a Concussion
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey (head) is currently out of the game and is being evaluated for a concussion, per Parker Gabriel. The 25-year-old might've suffered a concussion during the second half of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. It's unclear at the moment if Harvey is going to return to the contest. Before exiting, Harvey rushed the ball twice for six yards, but he has been doing more work in the receiving game. He has hauled in five of his six targets for 39 yards through the air. Rookie back Jonah Coleman (ankle) was placed on the Injured Reserve this week. J.K. Dobbins will be the lead back in Denver if Harvey is forced to miss time. Fantasy managers should stay tuned for more updates on his status.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Faces Hot Rams Run Defense in Week 3
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey has recovered from a hamstring injury that left him limited to begin the week of practice leading into Week 3 against the Los Angeles Rams. Harvey and Broncos lead running back, J.K. Dobbins, each returned to full practice on Thursday and Friday after being listed as limited participants on Wednesday. As a result, he has not been provided an injury designation entering this weekend's non-conference matchup. Harvey has carried the ball just three times this season but has averaged six yards per carry, while he has added four receptions for 23 yards. He hasn't been much of a factor offensively, but could see a boost as fellow running back Jonah Coleman is out for this week's game with an ankle injury. Harvey is RotoBaller's 45th-ranked running back and projected to score nine fantasy points against the Broncos' NFC foe. The Rams' defense did a nice job against New York Giants running backs last week, limiting starter Cam Skattebo to just 36 yards rushing on 12 carries and four receptions for 19 yards.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) will play Sunday
metadata.description: RJ Harvey (hamstring) will play in Sunday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: Harvey is set to make his return to the field in Week 3 after being sidelined for one game due to a hamstring issue. He should see a full workload against the Rams this week, especially with rookie Jonah Coleman (ankle) set to be sidelined in that matchup.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Will Return in Week 3
metadata.description: Denver Broncos second-year running back RJ Harvey (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday and Friday and has been cleared to play in Week 3 on Sunday Night Football against the Los Angeles Rams, according to the team. Harvey and the entire Broncos offense flopped in their Week 1 loss to the division-rival Kansas City Chiefs, with Harvey carrying the ball three times for 18 yards and catching all four of his targets for 23 yards as a receiver. The 25-year-old former second-rounder from Central Florida picked up a hamstring injury in that game and did not play in the Week 2 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars. With a week to rest, he is ready to go this weekend against the visiting Rams, but Harvey will be a deep-league RB3/flex option, at best, with J.K. Dobbins recovered from a hip injury that he suffered this past Sunday. With rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman ruled out with an ankle injury, it could give Harvey a little more upside in point-per-reception leagues, but the matchup is not a great one against a Rams defense that is among the best in the league.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) upgraded to full participant Thursday
metadata.description: RJ Harvey (hamstring) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Harvey missed last week's game due to a hamstring injury that he has been dealing with, but he was able to return to a full practice on Thursday, so it seems likely that he will suit up and play in Week 3. He will likely continue to share the backfield with J.K. Dobbins (hip), though it looks like rookie Jonah Coleman (ankle) will be out of his hair for at least a week.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Upgrades to full practice
metadata.description: Harvey (hamstring) was listed as a full participant on Thursday's injury report.
metadata.analysis: Harvey missed Week 2 with a hamstring injury, but he got in a limited practice Wednesday and a full session a day later, so he is set to return to action Sunday against the Rams. Fellow running back J.K. Dobbins (hip) also practiced fully while Jonah Coleman (ankle) missed a second straight day of work, so Harvey may only need to share the snaps with one running back in Week 3 rather than two.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Getting Healthier, Returns to Full Practice
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey (hamstring) was upgraded to a full practice on Thursday after he was limited in the first practice of the week on Wednesday, according to the team. Harvey came out of the Week 1 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs with a hamstring injury and was held out this past Sunday in the Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. Fellow RB J.K. Dobbins dealt with hamstring cramping on Sunday and was pulled, but he has also been upgraded to a full practice and looks to be on track to play on Sunday night against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3. Rookie Jonah Coleman (ankle), who led the backfield against the Jags because of the injuries to Dobbins and Harvey, has yet to practice this week due to an ankle injury. While sharing the backfield in the season opener with Dobbins, Harvey played only 51% of the offensive snaps and carried the ball just three times for 18 yards. He did have four receptions for 23 yards through the air, though. Even if Coleman is not cleared to play this weekend, Harvey will be hard to recommend as a flex option against the Rams, even in deep PPR leagues.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Present for Thursday's practice
metadata.description: Harvey (hamstring) was spotted on the field for the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette reports.
metadata.analysis: After sitting out the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, Harvey opened Week 3 prep as a limited participant Wednesday. If he can upgrade to full activity Thursday, it would clear up any concern about his status heading into Sunday's game against the Rams. He's one of three Denver running backs on the injury report this week, as J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) was limited and Jonah Coleman (ankle) didn't participate in the team's first practice of the week.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Practices in limited capacity
metadata.description: Harvey (hamstring) was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Harvey sat out this past Sunday's win versus the Jaguars due to a hamstring injury, but going back to last week, he's now logged three straight 'limited' listings on Denver's practice reports. Meanwhile, J.K. Dobbins (hip) also was limited Wednesday, while Jonah Coleman sat out due to a sprained ankle. Considering the team's top three running backs currently are banged-up, the situation will continue to be monitored to get a sense of who among the three may be available Sunday against the Rams.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) listed as limited Wednesday
metadata.description: RJ Harvey (hamstring) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Harvey was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday after missing last week's game due to a hamstring injury. It looks like he's trending towards playing in Week 3 and could see more work than usual if Jonah Coleman (ankle) is ruled out ahead of the team's matchup against the Rams on Sunday night.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) seen practicing Wednesday
metadata.description: RJ Harvey (hamstring) was seen practicing for the Broncos on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The young running back was sidelined last week due to a hamstring injury, but it looks like he will have a chance to make his return to the lineup in Week 3, as he is participating in practice in some capacity to start the week on Wednesday. His potential return this week would mean less work for rookie Jonah Coleman (hamstring) moving forward.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Making progress in recovery
metadata.description: Harvey is continuing to make progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury that sidelined him for the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Harvey appears to have made some improvement heading into Week 3, but his practice participation Wednesday through Friday will ultimately determine whether he plays this Sunday against the Rams. The top three running backs on the Denver depth chart are all tending to injuries, as starter J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) made an early exit from this past Sunday's game, while rookie Jonah Coleman emerged from the contest with an ankle sprain.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Listed as Limited on Wednesday
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey (hamstring), who missed the team's Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, was listed as a limited participant in practice on Wednesday, per the team. The Broncos' backfield is banged up heading into a primetime Week 3 matchup at home against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday night. J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) left the Week 2 victory with hamstring cramping, and rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman is now dealing with an ankle injury. The Broncos' only other RB on the roster is Tyler Badie. Dobbins might have the best chance of suiting up this weekend in Denver, but we probably will not have a clearer picture of how this backfield might shake out until later in the week. Harvey took over as Denver's lead back in his rookie campaign in 2025 after Dobbins' season-ending foot injury, but with Coleman in the fold this year, a clear path to a fantasy-relevant role is hard to see. The 25-year-old had just three carries for 18 yards in the season-opening loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and added four catches for 23 yards. Harvey's primary value comes as a PPR bench stash.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) inactive for Week 2
metadata.description: RJ Harvey (hamstring) is inactive for Week 2 for the Denver Broncos against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Harvey will not suit up after being unable to progress throughout the week for the Broncos. J.K. Dobbins will lead the Denver backfield attack with Jonah Coleman to see increased snaps against the Jaguars for head coach Sean Payton Sunday.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Inactive in Week 2
metadata.description: Harvey (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Susanna Weir of the Broncos' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Harvey opened Week 2 prep as a non-participant on the Broncos' initial injury report due to a hamstring issue, which he followed up with back-to-back limited sessions and a questionable designation entering the weekend. Having said that, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Sunday morning that Harvey was unlikely to play, and that's been confirmed as Denver posted its list of inactives. J.K. Dobbins will pace the backfield Sunday, while rookie Jonah Coleman and Tyler Badie also will be on hand for RB reps.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey Inactive Against Jaguars
metadata.description: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. Harvey was limited in practice Thursday and Friday after sitting out Wednesday and entered the weekend listed as questionable. He had three carries for 18 yards and caught four passes for 23 yards in the season opener against Kansas City. J.K. Dobbins remains Denver's lead back, while rookie Jonah Coleman and Tyler Badie move up the depth chart with Harvey unavailable. If Harvey's injury is significant enough to potentially keep him out beyond Week 2, Coleman should become a popular waiver-wire pickup at RB, especially if he has a large role on Sunday against the Jags.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) unlikely to play against Jags
metadata.description: RJ Harvey (hamstring) is unlikely to play against the Jaguars on Sunday due to a hamstring injury.
metadata.analysis: If Harvey sits, JK Dobbins will once again be the primary rusher and it will open up touches for Jonah Coleman, as he is a capable pass catcher. Dobbins is worth starting this week, and Coleman could be an interesting start in deeper formats.

metadata.title: RJ Harvey - Unlikely to play Sunday
metadata.description: Harvey (hamstring) "is unlikely to play" Sunday against the Jaguars, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Harvey was able to practice on a limited basis Thursday and Friday after sitting out Wednesday's session, but it appears he will not be able to give it a go in Week 2. The Broncos and Jaguars will not kick off until 4:05 p.m. ET, so unfortunately for fantasy players Harvey's availability for Sunday's game will not officially be revealed until after the early wave of games gets underway. Rookie Jonah Coleman could see more time behind J.K. Dobbins if Harvey is unable to suit up.
